[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Source for this information: The RW Pension application of Willoughby WILLIAMS (fn122NC),Davidson County, TN. Transcribed by Will Graves.

In March 1848, Nancy MCMINN appeared before the court of Davidson Co., TN to make a declaration in order to obtain pension benefits. Nancy made application as the widow of Willoughby WILLIAMS, and officer in the RW. She stated that her husband, Willoughby WILLIAMS, had entered the service in Dobbs Co., NC. Abram SHEPPARD was his COl, and George WASHINGTON his Gen. She stated that Col. James GLASSCO, the Secretary of the State of NC, was her father and had served with Willoughby WILLIAMS in the RW. She md. WILLIAMS after the war on 1 Jan 1786.

Her husband, Willoughby WILLIAMS, died 6 June 1802 during their move from Greene Co., NC to the State of TN. They had four chldren. Two were J.G. and Willoughby WILLIAMS. Their son, Willoughby WILLIAMS md. Nancy GLASSCO whose 6th child, also a Willoughby WIlliams, b. June 14, 1798 was living in Nashville, TN in 1851.

Widow Nancy GLASSCO WILLIAMS md. Joseph MCMINN, Esq. in August of 1816. Nancy MCMINN died 27 Jun 1857. Joseph died 17 Nov 1824. Joseph had served as Governor of Tennessee from 1815 to 1821.

=== Current held-family review, 23 October 2026 ===

'''Existing father 73% → 96% confident.''' Holloman’s inspected NCpedia biography names daughter Nancy Ann (Annie), gives 22 April 1770, identifies Willoughby Williams as the secretary’s son-in-law and describes his death during the Tennessee migration. Nancy’s complete captured biography identifies both Williams and Governor Joseph McMinn as her husbands and reports that her March 1848 pension declaration named Colonel James Glassco, North Carolina secretary of state, as her father. The distinctive two-husband sequence and reported father’s exact public role identify this adult Nancy, rather than merely a same-name daughter.

96% concerns the complete existing Nancy-to-Secretary-James profile pair. The pension father statement is held through the captured biography, not an inspected original pension or Graves transcription. The First Ladies book remains an uninspected citation. Holloman’s 1770 and the profile’s 1771 birth years differ by one year despite matching day/month; Dandridge/Rutledge death locality and May/August 1816 remarriage details remain unresolved. These accounts may be dependent. Existing vitals, mothers and spouses are retained; no new attachment or live edit.
